data.name: Amila
data.gender_notes: Amila is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is sweet in speech and manner. The name Amila carries the meaning “Sweetness” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Amila usually hope their child will grow to embody sweetness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name given to a child who is expected to be sweet and gentle in her speech and actions, embodying the virtues of kindness and grace
data.etymology: Amila belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sweetness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amila total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: عميلى
in_arabic.meaning: عميلى تعني العاملة أو القائمة بالأعمال الصالحة
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم عميلى مشتق من الجذر العربي 'ع-م-ل' والذي يعني العمل أو القيام بالأعمال. في اللغة العربية، تعني العميلى المرأة العاملة أو القائمة بالأعمال الصالحة. وقد ورد هذا الجذر في القرآن الكريم في عدة آيات، منها قوله تعالى 'وَمَا أَفْعَلُ بِهَذِهِ الْعَمَلَةِ' (الأنعام: 119)، حيث يشير إلى العمل الصالح والنية الطيبة.

in_urdu.name: عمیلی
in_urdu.meaning: عمیلی کا مطلب ہے مہنگی یا اچھی کارکردگی کرنے والی
in_urdu.long_meaning: عمیلی نام عربی زبان کے 'ع-م-ل' جذر سے نکلا ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے کام کرنا یا عمل کرنا۔ اردو میں، عمیلی کا نام ان نساء کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو اچھی کارکردگی یا مہنگی کام کرنے والی ہوتی ہیں۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمان معاشرے میں مقبول ہے، جہاں یہ دینی اور ثقافتی اہمیت رکھتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: अमीली
in_hindi.meaning: अमीली का अर्थ है परिश्रम करने वाली या उत्तम कार्य करने वाली
in_hindi.long_meaning: अमीली नाम की उत्पत्ति العربية भाषा के 'ع-م-ل' मूल से हुई है, जिसका अर्थ है काम करना या क्रिया करना। हिन्दी मुस्लिम समुदाय में, अमीली नाम का अर्थ है परिश्रम करने वाली या उत्तम कार्य करने वाली। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम परंपरा में महत्वपूर्ण है, जहां यह आध्यात्मिक और नैतिक मूल्यों को दर्शाता है।

in_english.name: Amila
in_english.meaning: Amila means worker or one who performs good deeds
in_english.long_meaning: The name Amila is derived from the Arabic root 'ع-م-ل' (ʿ-m-l), which means 'to work' or 'to do'. In Islamic tradition, Amila refers to a woman who is diligent in her work or one who performs good deeds. This root appears in several Quranic verses, including 'And what I do not do with this action' (6:119), highlighting the importance of intention and righteous deeds. The name Amila is used across various Muslim cultures, symbolizing diligence, piety, and good character.

data.cultural_impact: The name Amila holds a significant cultural impact as it is derived from the Arabic language, which is the primary language of the Islamic faith. It translates to 'One who is sweet in speech and manner', implying kindness, good-naturedness, and consideration towards others. In many Islamic cultures, a person's character is highly valued, and the name Amila reflects the desirable qualities that individuals endeavor to cultivate.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, the name Amila holds great significance as it embodies the virtues of kindness, compassion, and good character. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) once said that "Indeed, good manners are a part of faith." (Bukhari and Muslim). The name Amila serves as a daily reminder to practice gentle speech and good behavior towards others, emphasizing the importance of treating people with respect and dignity, which is deeply rooted in Islamic teachings. The name thus acts as a spiritual anchor that encourages individuals to stay true to their faith by being good and kind to themselves and others.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Sweetness" symbolizes One who is sweet in speech and manner. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Amila serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of sweetness.
